painGuide.title: Pain & Adjustments
painGuide.subtitle: Troubleshooting guide — quick fixes by pain zone
painGuide.disclaimer: Apply these tips once the equipment has been checked. They are not a substitute for a comprehensive assessment by a healthcare professional.

c0.s0: Go up a shoe size or loosen the straps
c0.s1: Use wider shoes ("wide" models: Shimano, Lake, Specialized)
c0.s2: Thinner or custom insoles made by a sports podiatrist

c0.p: Shoe too tight with the tongue pressing on the area (pedal at top or excessive dorsiflexion)
c0.s0: Replace shoes with a more open model at that point (e.g. Lake brand)
c0.s1: Cut part of the tongue with scissors (common with Sidi shoes)
c0.s2: Thinner or custom insoles from a sports podiatrist
c0.s3: Review cleat position (too far forward) and saddle height (too low): the ankle may be working through a poor range of motion

c0.p: Excessive pressure on the outer edge of the foot or another maximum pressure point
c0.s0: Shoes too tight or too narrow at the front — use "wide" shoes
c0.s1: Custom insoles from a sports podiatrist
c0.s2: Move cleats toward the inside of the shoe to push the feet away from the cranks

c0.s0: Go up a shoe size or loosen the straps

c1.p: Feet not held firmly enough (toes work harder to maintain stability)
c1.s0: Go down a shoe size, thicker or custom insoles
c1.s2: Engage the foot more (move cleat toward the heel)

c2.p: Incorrectly adjusted cleats or saddle too low
c2.s0: Review cleat engagement (often too far forward)

c3.s0: Replace shoes with a model better suited to your foot morphology

c0.s0: Review cleat position (often too far forward)
c0.s2: Engage the foot more (move cleat toward the heel)

c1.s0: Replace shoes with a model that does not press on the tendon

c2.p: Lots of positive elevation (low cadence, greater ankle mobilisation) or excessive force work
c2.s0: Reduce training volume, especially force work and hilly routes
c2.s2: Raise the saddle to the optimal angle for your discipline

c0.p: Excessive quadriceps load, too much knee flexion
c0.s0: Raise and/or move the saddle back
c0.s2: Engage the foot more (move cleat toward the heel)
c0.s3: Reduce training volume, especially force work and hilly routes

c0.p: Excessive hamstring load (too much knee extension)
c0.s2: Saddle-to-bar distance too great: shorten the stem
c0.s4: Rotate the cleat to bring the heel closer to the frame
c0.s5: Replace worn cleats and/or pedals — reduce float if adjustable

c1.p: Excessive external foot rotation (heel too close to the frame)
c1.s0: Rotate the cleat to move the heel away from the frame
c1.s1: Replace worn cleats and/or pedals — reduce float if adjustable

c2.p: Feet too far from the frame
c2.s0: Reduce Q-factor: move cleats toward the outside of the shoes to bring the feet closer to the cranks

c0.p: Excessive stress on the inner edge of the kneecap
c0.s0: Reduce training volume, especially force work and hilly routes
c0.s2: Saddle too low or too far forward: correct the height
c0.s3: Rotate the cleat to bring the heel closer to the frame

c1.p: Femoro-patellar dysplasia or other structural cause

c0.p: Excessive stress on the outer edge of the kneecap (same logic as the inner side)
c0.s0: Reduce training volume, especially force work and hilly routes
c0.s2: Saddle too low or too far forward: correct the height
c0.s3: Rotate the cleat to move the heel away from the frame (opposite to inner side)

c0.p: Excessive internal foot rotation (heel too far from the frame)
c0.s0: Rotate the cleat to bring the heel closer to the frame
c0.s1: Replace worn cleats and/or pedals — reduce float if adjustable

c1.p: Ankle too free / feet too close to the frame
c1.s0: Increase Q-factor: move cleats toward the inside of the shoes to push the feet further from the cranks
c1.s1: If insufficient, use spacers or pedals with a longer axle

c2.p: IT-band friction caused by incorrect saddle height

c0.s0: Lower the saddle to the optimal angle for your discipline

c1.p: Excessive range of motion or poor hip/knee/ankle alignment

c2.p: Pelvic compensation due to lower-limb asymmetry
c2.s0: Identify the cause of the asymmetry with a podiatrist
c2.s1: Orient the cleat of the inward-turning knee outward to restore alignment (move heel closer to the crank)
c2.s2: Leg length discrepancy: consult a podiatrist for a precise diagnosis

c3.p: Hip dysplasia or other structural cause

c0.p: Posterior muscle chain under too much tension / torso too far forward
c0.s2: Lower the saddle (and possibly move it forward)

c1.p: Torso too far back (posterior pelvic tilt)
c1.s1: Use a better-suited saddle (wide and short models for more stability)

c2.s0: Saddle too high or too far back: correct height and setback
c2.s3: Leg length discrepancy: consult a podiatrist for a precise diagnosis

c0.p: Too much pressure on the front and nose of the saddle / pelvis rotated too far forward
Too much pressure at the rear — saddle tilted too far back

c1.s0: Use a narrower saddle, particularly at the nose

c0.s2: Tilt the saddle nose up slightly
c0.s3: Shorten the stem and move the saddle back

c0.p: Too much weight on the arms (excessive forward reach)
c0.s1: Shorten the stem and move the saddle back

c2.s0: Widen the handlebar (= width between the two acromions)

c3.p: Excessive cervical tension compressing nerve roots
c3.s2: Many other possible causes — see a specialist if symptoms persist

c0.p: Too much weight on the wrists

c1.s0: Shorten the stem if the bars are hard to reach

c2.s0: Try a different bar tape model
c2.s1: Use two layers of bar tape to absorb vibrations

c3.s0: Narrow the handlebar (= width between the two acromions)

help.title: User guide
help.tool_pan_desc: Drag to pan the view (zoom > 1). Temporarily activate with Space.
help.tool_select_desc: Click to select an element, drag its handles to edit. Del/⌫ to delete.
help.tool_line_desc: Click and drag to draw an annotated straight line.
help.tool_angle_desc: 3 clicks: 1st point → vertex → 3rd point. Arc and degree value appear automatically. Colour advances automatically.
help.shortcut_space: Temporary pan — release to restore active tool
help.shortcut_shift: Go back / forward 10 frames at once
help.mouse_seekbar: Jump to that point in the video
help.split_desc1: Each panel A / B has its own independent layers, zoom, and pan.
help.split_desc2: Click a panel to activate it — tools and layers apply to it.
help.split_desc3: ← → and SHIFT+← → advance/rewind the active panel's video.
help.layers_desc2: Opacity slider 0–100% per layer · each stroke automatically creates its own layer.
help.media_capture_desc: Button at the bottom-right of each pane — saves the frame with all visible annotations.
help.media_panel_desc: Opens the media library at the bottom. Opens automatically when a new capture or recording is created.
help.media_view_desc: Displays the capture full-screen in the active pane (or pane B in split mode).
help.media_rename_desc: Renames the capture or video (display label only — the file on disk is not renamed).
help.media_import_desc: Opens a video file (WebM, MP4, MOV) or image (PNG, JPG, WebP) from disk.
help.media_source_desc: The dropdown above each pane lists cameras, videos and captures — selecting a capture displays it directly.
help.cotes_desc1: The right sidebar lists reference measurements for the active client's discipline.
help.cotes_desc2: Clicking a row selects it and shows the closest measured angle (green/orange/red badge).
help.cotes_desc3: The layer containing the matching angle is automatically renamed with the measurement name — undo with Ctrl+Z.
help.report_desc1: Report button in the header — 7 accordion sections: client info, profile, diagnosis, physio tests, assessment, measurements, captures.
help.report_desc2: Auto-save writes the form to report.json 800 ms after each edit.
help.report_desc3: Export PDF generates a structured document with company header, bike diagram, measurement tables and selected captures.
help.tool_skeleton_desc: Place anatomical joints on the video. Start tracking (⊙ button) to animate them automatically frame by frame.
help.tool_trajectory_desc: Click on a point in the video to start tracking it — one layer is created automatically per trajectory.
help.tracking_skeleton_desc1: ⊙ button at the bottom-right of the pane — only active when the layer contains a skeleton.
help.tracking_skeleton_desc2: Tracking pauses automatically when the video is paused and resumes on play. Each joint shows its confidence: orange ring = uncertain, pulsing red = recently lost, solid red = definitively lost.
help.tracking_skeleton_desc3: Drag a joint to reposition it live — the worker is reseeded immediately. Double-click a definitively lost joint to reseed it from the drawn skeleton position.
help.tracking_trajectory_desc1: T tool (Trajectory) — click on the video to place a tracking point. Multiple clicks = multiple simultaneous trajectories.
help.tracking_trajectory_desc2: The trajectory displays in real time with a colour drift (lightens over ~60 s). Hiding/showing the layer does not erase the trail.
help.tracking_trajectory_desc3: Once 20 points are accumulated, a dashed PCA ellipse appears with its circularity score (100% = perfect circle) and point count.
